Classic Halloween Candy Apples

Served at: All Hallows' Eve (Halloween)

Makes 6-8 candy applesPrep 20 minCook 15 min

Candy apples are a quintessential treat for All Hallows' Eve, their vibrant red sheen and crisp, sweet-tart bite embodying the spirit of autumn and festive fun. These iconic confections, often enjoyed at carnivals and fairs, become a special homemade delight during Halloween, perfect for parties or as a nostalgic seasonal indulgence.

Ingredients

  • 6-8 small to medium firm apples (such as Granny Smith or Fuji)
  • 6-8 wooden candy apple sticks or skewers
  • 2 cups (400 g) granulated sugar
  • 1 cup (240 ml) light corn syrup
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) water
  • 1 teaspoon (5 ml) red food coloring (gel or liquid)
  • 1/2 teaspoon (2.5 ml) vanilla extract (optional)
  • Parchment paper or silicone baking mat

Method

  1. Thoroughly wash and dry the apples. It is crucial that the apples are completely dry for the candy coating to adhere properly. Remove any stems.
  2. Insert a wooden candy apple stick or skewer firmly into the core of each apple, about two-thirds of the way through.
  3. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone baking mat and lightly grease it with cooking spray or butter. Set aside.
  4. In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine the granulated sugar, light corn syrup, and water. Stir gently over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
  5. Once the sugar is dissolved, increase the heat to medium-high and bring the mixture to a boil. Do not stir the mixture once it begins to boil, as this can cause crystallization.
  6. Insert a candy thermometer into the mixture, ensuring it does not touch the bottom of the pan. Continue to boil until the temperature reaches 300-310°F (149-154°C), which is the hard crack stage.
  7. Carefully remove the saucepan from the heat. Stir in the red food coloring and vanilla extract (if using) until evenly distributed. Work quickly as the candy will begin to cool and thicken.
  8. Tilt the saucepan slightly to pool the candy mixture. Carefully dip each apple into the hot candy, rotating it to ensure an even and complete coating. Allow any excess candy to drip off back into the pan.
  9. Place each coated apple onto the prepared baking sheet. Allow the candy apples to cool completely at room temperature for at least 30-60 minutes, or until the candy shell is hard and firm.
  10. Once cooled, serve immediately or store individually wrapped in cellophane at room temperature for up to 2-3 days.

Tips

  • Ensure apples are completely dry and free of wax (a quick dip in boiling water for a few seconds can help remove wax, then dry thoroughly).
  • Use a heavy-bottomed saucepan to prevent scorching and ensure even heating of the candy mixture.
  • For extra crunch, roll the freshly dipped candy apples in chopped nuts, sprinkles, or crushed cookies before the candy hardens.
